correctness.rationale: Free amalgamation cannot create a directed 3-cycle using vertices from both sides outside the base, and the limit realizes each admissible new-vertex diagram. Its finite relational homogeneity identifies exactly the equal diagrams over the named path. An old arc i→j closes a directed triangle precisely with x→i and j→x; an old nonedge imposes no constraint. The resulting consecutive-pair exclusions give exactly the stated transfer expression and biweight refinement. Path reversal reverses and complements the word and arc converse complements it, so all relevant equivalence classes are the four-image orbits (with repetitions allowed). The independent exact ternary enumeration for every orientation through eight gives class counts 1,1,2,3,6,10,20,36 and distinct profile counts 1,1,2,3,6,10,20,35. The sole double fibre has the displayed words, coefficient vector (1,16,105,368,753,923,664,257,41), and total 3,128; the biweight coefficients at (3,3) are 163 and 164. An isolated named point supplies an independent factor 1+2z, and the connected path remains identifiable as a component, so padded bases remain distinct.
residual_risks: No minimality assertion for arbitrary disconnected bases, no connected persistence beyond eight, and no classification without quotienting by converse are certified.

value.rationale: The adjacency degree of a fresh vertex is a natural coarsening of exact named type data; the path family removes unrelated differences in the undirected base and tests how much arc orientation that coarsening retains. The exhaustive first collision, its uniqueness and its separation under the natural split into in/out incidences answer that inverse question more informatively than a transfer formula or a single pair. Padding shows that the obstruction persists among finite bases, without claiming connected persistence.
residual_risks: The value is specific to this induced-path reconstruction problem; no general classification for all forbidden-cycle bases is claimed.
